text:
maria_cs: Customer acme-inc opened a support case — they're getting 429s from the API but the Console quota panel shows ~1.5M tokens remaining. Customer started hitting errors around 11:40am UTC. Can infra take a look? :eyes:

alerts-bot: alert: spike(429) detected for tenant=acme-inc (rate-limit-enforcer). 120 errors in last 5m.

nate_sre: thanks. can you paste an example request + response and the request-id from the customer? also which org/tenant id?

maria_cs: tenant=acme-inc, request-id: rQ_3bK9X. curl they used:```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-..." \
  -H "X-Request-ID: rQ_3bK9X" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-large","input":"hello"}'
```
response: HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
{"error":"quota_exceeded","message":"quota exhausted for tenant","code":429}

eli_backend: I'm looking at enforcer logs for that tenant. timestamped entries show enforcer returned 429 due to `available_tokens <= 0`. Example log: `enforcer tenant=acme-inc available=0 last_deduct=1805123000`

sam_product: but the Console UI for acme-inc shows `remaining_tokens: 1500000` in the quota panel. So UI and enforcer disagree.

zoe_engineering: likely split between the metrics pipeline (used by Console) and the authoritative quota-store used by enforcer. Console reads aggregated metrics in ClickHouse (near-real-time batch), enforcer reads Redis-based quota state. If the aggregator is lagging, UI can show stale higher tokens.

nate_sre: can someone check Redis for `quota:acme-inc:tokens` now? and check the aggregator consumer lag (kafka consumer group: quota-aggregator-prod)?

eli_backend: checked Redis: `GET quota:acme-inc:tokens` -> `0` (integer). TTL 30s. Also found recent incremental writes to aggregator topic blocked: `quota-aggregator` consumer lag = 120k messages, consumer group lag spiked at 11:35am.

maria_cs: customer timeline: they had a big burst at 11:30-11:42 after a scheduled job. Errors started 11:40. They saw UI before 11:45 and reported the mismatch.

zoe_engineering: root cause hypothesis: a backlog in the aggregator consumer (Kafka) prevented the batch job that pushes the latest consumption metrics to ClickHouse. ClickHouse (Console) still showing pre-burst snapshot -> inflated remaining tokens. Meanwhile the enforcer (Redis token decrementer) was operating in realtime and depleted tokens. So enforcement is correct, UI stale.

nate_sre: mitigation options: 1) catch up consumer (but that takes time), 2) force a full refresh push of the latest aggregated state to ClickHouse for affected tenants, 3) temporarily whitelist/lift enforcement for acme-inc while we fix pipeline. Thoughts?

eli_backend: We can push a small script to rehydrate ClickHouse for acme-inc from the quota-store (Redis) immediately. That'll make UI reflect current state. I can run it now for this tenant.

sam_product: customer asked for quick fix to stop 429s — they are production traffic. If we lift enforcement it may let them continue while we fix the pipeline. However that's risky for other tenants. Prefer to update Console first so CS has accurate view and then coordinate with customer.

maria_cs: customer prefers immediate relief. They asked: can you open a temporary override while you fix the metrics so they can finish their job?

nate_sre: I'll approve a one-hour soft-limit override for tenant=acme-inc, but only if we add alerting to roll it back automatically and document in incident. eli, can you push the ClickHouse refresh now? I'll open the override once you confirm the refresh ran.

eli_backend: running rehydrate script now:```bash
python tools/rehydrate_console.py --tenant acme-inc --source redis --target clickhouse
```
output: `rehydrate completed for tenant=acme-inc; clickhouse updated at 1805123550; remaining_tokens=0`

nate_sre: got confirmation. Console now shows 0 remaining tokens (matches enforcer). Proceeding to create a one-hour override in enforcement-admin: `POST /admin/overrides` body: {tenant:"acme-inc", override_tokens: 500000, ttl_seconds:3600, reason:"support temporary lift"}

eli_backend: override accepted by admin API. enforcement logs now show `applied override +500000 tokens for tenant=acme-inc until 1805127220`. 429s should stop.

maria_cs: relaying to customer: applied 500k temporary credits for 1h. Please continue and tell us if you see more 429s.

sam_product: next steps: (1) fix quota-aggregator consumer lag root cause (investigate why it spiked), (2) add end-to-end consistency checks between ClickHouse snapshots and Redis quota-store (daily job + alert when drift > X), (3) postmortem and customer comms.

zoe_engineering: initial consumer metrics: consumer restarted once at 11:33 due to OOM (killed by kube). Need to check memory/regulator and bump replicas or fix leak.

nate_sre: assigning eng-runtime to own the RCA. I'll open an incident in #incidents and tag eng-runtime + eng-ml (for heavy batch loads).

maria_cs: I'll update the support ticket and confirm customer can continue. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

zoe_engineering: filing follow-up tickets: PROD-1182 (consumer OOM fix), PROD-1183 (drift alert), PROD-1184 (add tenant-level reconciliation).

eli_backend: leaving logs and the rehydrate script run in the incident for auditors.

nate_sre: closing this Slack thread — moving discussion to incident channel. If anyone needs anything else ping me.
